feeds.title: Words Matter
feeds.description: Words Matter is an English Literature Blog by York St John University.Here at York St John, our approach to Literature is simple: words matter. Words shape the world we live in, books can and have changed the world and the connections between the written page and the concerns of the 'real' world are a crucial part of our work. Our blog celebrates this philosophy.

feeds.title: Times Literary Supplement » Literature
feeds.description: Essays and reviews on the latest fiction in English and in translation, exploring literature, poetry, prose, and criticism from across the world and across the centuries.TLS is the leading journal for literary culture, the Times Literary Supplement is a weekly review of books and the arts, founded in 1902.

feeds.title: Books and Bao » Literature
feeds.description: Read our reviews of translated literature, author spotlights, essays, and translator interviews to discover something new.Books and Bao helps in blending literature and culture-based travel, we specialise and promote diverse books from around the world. We spotlight literature in translation, LGBTQ authors and stories, and writers of colour.

feeds.title: Readings : Free English Literature Notes
feeds.description: Read articles on Canadian literature, post colonial literature, Dalit literature, and more on the Free English Literature Notes Blog.Mr. Abdul Samad K teaches English language and literature at PSMO College Tirurangadi and he is currently pursuing his PhD.

feeds.title: The Modern Novel Blog
feeds.description: Reviews and more about the worldwide modern literary novel.

feeds.title: The New Inquiry
feeds.description: The New Inquiry is a space for discussion that aspires to enrich cultural, literature and public life by putting all available resources: both digital and material towards the promotion and exploration of ideas.

feeds.title: English Blog
feeds.description: I am Anupriya Ahmed, mentor of this blog. I welcome you to this wonderful blog on the English language and literature. I completed my Masters in English literature and took up the profession of teaching. I am here to help learners build knowledge of the content and methods of the Language and literature.

feeds.title: Literature Cambridge
feeds.description: Literature Cambridge is an independent educational organisation providing top quality courses on the best of English literature. Their courses are taught by leading academics and are open to all.

feeds.title: English Literature Made Easy for Students
feeds.description: I am Shish Pal Chauhan. I have worked as a lecturer in English and a principal at a Senior Secondary School. This blog is for the students who wish to read and understand English Literature made easy. The students will find discussion on poems, short stories, novels, plays and literary essays. line-to-line explanation of the poems, dramas, questions & answers, etc.

feeds.title: English literature and linguistics with Asma Sheikh
feeds.description: I am Asma Sheikh, Pakistan's first female online tutor of English literature, I completed my Masters in English literature at the University of Punjab. This blog is solely dedicated to English literature students.

feeds.title: Literary Hub
feeds.description: The best of the literary web

feeds.title: Bloomsbury Literary Studies Blog
feeds.description: Bloomsbury presents a diverse collection of literary studies, covering modern writing, theory, and culture. From introductory texts for students to advanced research for scholars, including creative writing guides, our publications aim to advance scholarship and explore emerging fields like genre fiction and environmental literature. With the Object Lessons series, we encourage critical thinking across disciplines, reaffirming our commitment to innovative scholarship and expanding the boundaries of literary study.

feeds.title: A Year of Reading The World
feeds.description: Ann Morgan, a UK-based author, TED speaker, Royal Literary Fund fellow, and editor, is best known for her first book, 'Reading the World' (or 'The World Between Two Covers' in the US). This work was inspired by her year-long journey through a book from every country in the world, a remarkable adventure documented on her blog. In addition to her non-fiction work, Ann is the author of two novels: 'Beside Myself' and 'Crossing Over.'

feeds.title: ImoReads » English literature
feeds.description: Posts about English literature written by imoreads97

feeds.title: Electric Literature
feeds.description: Electric Literature is a nonprofit digital publisher with the mission to make literature more exciting, relevant, and inclusive. We are committed to publishing work that is intelligent and unpretentious, elevating new voices, and examining how literature and storytelling can help illuminate social justice issues and current events.

feeds.title: A Little Blog of Books
feeds.description: A Little Blog of Books is focused around Clare's favourite genres - contemporary, literary and translated fiction. The blog has detailed reviews split by A-Z and year, a list of the books to be read, and a variety of literature news and feature pieces.

feeds.title: Blog of English Literature
feeds.description: Read, learn and prosper.

feeds.title: Swifterature
feeds.description: I'm a professor of English Literature at Ghent University, Belgium. A lifelong Swiftie, I started this blog to document and explore the increasingly literary quality of Swift's songwriting. This has been the subject of increasing media attention since the release of albums folklore and evermore,literawhich marked Swift's foray into increasingly experimental songwriting territory and which were marketed around the idea of being unable to stop telling stories

feeds.title: The Assimilators
feeds.description: Get the PDFs of easily explained notes, short questions and long answers of MA English Literature of Sargodha University.The Assimilators is a go-to place for your literary ease. We provide simple and easy-to-understand posts along with references so that you can easily get in touch with a broader range of knowledge.

feeds.title: ElifNotes » Literature
feeds.description: ElifNotes is an educational website that focuses on providing literary help including English literature notes, book summaries, their analysis and reviews. We foster all enthusiastic learners by providing well-researched, self-created and plagiarism-free content.

feeds.title: Literarism
feeds.description: Literarism covers articles on Anglo Norman, Anglo Saxon, Augustan, Chaucer Age, Elizabethan, modern literature, post modern, Puritan, Victorian and more. It is based on different sources from magazines or newspapers.

feeds.title: HTMLGIANT
feeds.description: HTMLGIANT is an online literature blog founded by American author Blake Butler. Covers articles on poems, poetry, satire, reviews and other literature.

feeds.title: Dr. Vijayalayan's Literature Notes
feeds.description: Dr. Vijayalayan is a professor of English Literature at RKM Vivekananda College, Chennai. This blog is intended to create a repository of knowledge that can be accessed by students as both stand-alone information and as documentation of notes and addendums to the lessons taught in class.

feeds.title: Raju's English Literature Blog
feeds.description: Raju's English Literature Blog covers articles on poetry, novel, drama, essay, short stories, criticism & theory, Shakespeare, and more.

feeds.title: English Literature
feeds.description: I'm Samia Umer from Islamabad, Pakistan. I'm a qualified English Literature lecturer and an emerging blogger of English literature and Linguistics. My sole aim is to help the students of English literature by providing them with best possible notes and videos of my lectures. This blog will be filled with my handwritten notes and all sorts of beneficial posts regarding English literature.

feeds.title: The Conversation » English literature
feeds.description: Browse the latest English Literature news, research and analysis fromThe Conversation.The Conversation is a collaboration between editors and academics to provide informed news analysis and commentary that's free to read and republish.

feeds.title: British Council Arts
feeds.description: These blog posts offer an insight into some of the projects that we've supported and how the British Council works with literature, including interviews with writers, diaries from international visits, and reflections on completed or on-going projects.The British Council was founded to create 'a friendly knowledge and understanding' between the people of the UK and the wider world.

feeds.title: English Literature24
feeds.description: We created EnglishLiterature24 to support aspiring students around the world. This blog is dedicated to the learners of English Literature.Our website is updated daily to provide learners with unique articles.
